messages.content: The Hyatt just emailed that its main beachfront pool will be closed for maintenance during part of our stay. Please verify the exact dates and what will still be open. Our cancellation deadline is in six days, so I need a real comparison before then.

I confirmed the closure directly with the resort. The main lagoon-style beachfront pool is scheduled to close from Monday, February 23 through Thursday, February 26, reopening at 8:00 a.m. Friday, February 27. The beach remains accessible, and the smaller quiet pool, fitness center, spa, restaurants, and beach services are expected to operate normally. The pool bar will close with the main pool, but food and drinks can be ordered at the quiet pool. The resort says the work is contained to the pool deck, though some daytime construction noise may carry to nearby outdoor areas.
Is the quiet pool genuinely usable by all hotel guests, or is it tied to a room category? And does the spa have a hot tub or another soaking area we can use without buying treatments?

The quiet pool is available to all registered guests and does not require a club or suite booking. It has loungers and towel service, but it is substantially smaller and has no swim-up bar. The fitness center remains open 24 hours. The spa has a hot tub within its wet facilities, but access is included only on a treatment day; otherwise a day pass is $65 per person, subject to capacity. Your two Tuesday massages include spa-facility access that day.
Ask Hyatt what they will offer us in writing. Four days is more than a minor inconvenience, especially when the closed pool was a major reason for choosing the property.

Hyatt has offered a $600 resort credit if you keep the reservation. It would be separate from the existing $100 package credit, could be applied to eligible dining or spa charges, and would not cover room rate, taxes, gratuities, or outside operators. They also offered penalty-free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. AST on February 7, preserving the existing deadline. I requested written confirmation of the closure dates, remaining facilities, and credit terms; the guest-relations representative has sent it by email and added the same terms to the reservation notes.
Good. What is the nearby alternative that became available? Compare the actual room, all-in lodging total, pool situation, gym, hot tub, and cancellation terms. Do not hold it yet.

The available alternative is The St. Regis Bahia Beach, about 15 minutes from the Hyatt. Its Deluxe Ocean View King is available February 21-28 for $6,428.70 including taxes and the destination fee. It has a balcony, but the view can be partial through landscaping. The resort confirms its beachfront pool is fully open, the fitness center is on site, and the spa has a hot tub available only with a treatment or paid spa pass. The rate requires a $918.39 one-night deposit and permits cancellation without penalty through 6:00 p.m. AST on February 3; after that, the deposit is forfeited. Breakfast is not included.
So compare that against what remains payable at Hyatt after the new credit. Include breakfast and our massages correctly rather than treating every credit as cash off the room.

Hyatt lodging remains $5,185.84, of which $1,481.67 is already paid and $3,704.17 remains due. The two massages total $444. The original $100 package credit and new $600 disruption credit can both be applied to eligible spa and dining charges, so the massages could be fully covered and $256 of credit would remain for dining. Breakfast for two is included daily. St. Regis lodging would be $6,428.70; comparable breakfast for two for seven mornings is approximately $630 including service and tax, and replacing the massages at current St. Regis pricing would be $570 including service charges. That produces a comparable St. Regis property total of about $7,628.70, versus $5,629.84 in Hyatt lodging plus massages before applying Hyatt's $700 in credits. The effective difference is about $2,698.86 when the usable Hyatt credits and included breakfast are recognized.
Now account for everything that would have to move. Start with the private airport transfer.

The transfer company can change both rides to St. Regis. Because it is in a different service zone, the round-trip price would rise from the $356 already paid to $404, requiring an additional $48. There is no amendment fee if changed by February 10. The February 21 airport pickup can remain at 1:45 p.m.; the February 28 hotel pickup would move from 10:45 to 10:30 a.m. because of the longer drive.
And the rental delivery plus Thursday's El Yunque pickup? I do not want to discover later that either reservation is invalid.

Enterprise can deliver the midsize car to St. Regis on Wednesday, February 25, but adds a $35 location charge. The 8:30 a.m. delivery and 7:00 p.m. collection remain available, making the rental $186 payable at pickup. The El Yunque operator serves St. Regis without a surcharge. Pickup would change from 7:15 to 7:00 a.m., with the same approximate 1:30 p.m. return. The $398 tour price and its February 23 cancellation deadline would remain unchanged.
Are the Hyatt massage appointments transferable?

No. The Hyatt appointments would have to be canceled and replaced at St. Regis. Hyatt permits penalty-free cancellation until 2:00 p.m. AST on February 23. St. Regis currently has two separate 50-minute massages available Tuesday at 2:15 p.m., totaling $570, but availability is not guaranteed unless booked.
Please give me the clean incremental cost of moving, including the transport and rental changes, but not the tour since its price is unchanged.

Using comparable lodging, seven breakfasts, and two massages, St. Regis is approximately $2,698.86 more than keeping Hyatt and fully using Hyatt's $700 in credits. The transfer increase is $48 and the rental delivery increase is $35. The estimated incremental cost to relocate is therefore $2,781.86. The Delta tickets and $398 tour do not change. St. Regis food pricing or unused Hyatt credits could shift the realized difference.

The main pool closure is disappointing, but we will still have a pool and an on-site fitness center at Hyatt, and the spa hot tub on massage day. That combination matters more to us than having the larger pool every day, and the alternative is too large a premium. Keep Hyatt if the $600 credit is firmly documented and does not replace the original $100 credit.

The written offer expressly states that the $600 disruption credit is additional to the $100 credit included in your package. Both remain attached to the reservation, for $700 total in eligible dining-and-spa credits. The email also confirms the February 23-26 main-pool closure, access to the quiet pool for all registered guests, continued 24-hour fitness-center operation, and your existing penalty-free cancellation deadline of 11:59 p.m. AST on February 7.
Before I commit, confirm whether accepting that credit waives our right to complain if the quiet pool or beach also closes unexpectedly.

It does not. The written terms say the credit resolves the announced main-pool maintenance only. They do not waive remedies for a separate material facility closure, and there is no release or non-disparagement language. Any weather closure would still fall under the property's normal policies rather than this maintenance accommodation.
Then accept the $600 credit and retain the Hyatt reservation. Send me a concise final accounting and make no changes to the transfer, rental, tour, flights, or massages.

The $600 disruption credit has been accepted and Hyatt remains confirmed for February 21-28. It is documented as additional to the package's $100 credit, giving you $700 total for eligible dining and spa charges. Lodging remains $5,185.84: $1,481.67 paid and $3,704.17 due at the property. The two Hyatt massages remain Tuesday at 2:00 p.m. for $444 before credits, so they can be fully covered, leaving up to $256 for eligible dining. The main pool is scheduled to close February 23-26; the quiet pool, beach, fitness center, spa, and restaurants remain available as described. Your February 7 at 11:59 p.m. AST cancellation deadline is unchanged. No St. Regis reservation was made, and no changes were made to the Delta flights, $356 private transfer, $151 Enterprise rental, $398 El Yunque tour, or massage appointments.
